cand.title: Velo-city 2028 Geneva
cand.organizationName: European Cyclists’ Federation with Geneva host city
cand.excerpt: High evidence and date quality; ranking tempered where venue is already committed or hotel access is unconfirmed.

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Primary relationship candidates: Anouk Rey, Managing Director, K.I.T. Group Switzerland, quoted specifically as the partnering PCO; Caroline Cerfontaine, ECF Director Velo-city, the event-owner conference lead. Local introductions: David Cougoule, Senior Manager, Geneva Convention Bureau, quoted in the host announcement; Mégane Simeon, Bid & Communication Manager, the edition press release’s named bureau contact. These are commercially relevant contacts, not verified hotel-contract signatories.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced Geneva edition: 13–16 June 2028, within the requested horizon. These are conference activity dates, not publication dates. The April 2025 host announcement and official FAQ agree. The next series edition before Geneva is Matsuyama/Ehime, 25–28 May 2027, at Ehime Prefectural Budokan; it is not a Geneva lodging opportunity.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel brief: YOTEL Geneva Lake is a conditional airport-corridor satellite, not the congress venue or default primary housing. Its 237 rooms and approximately 250-theatre maximum do not support hosting this roughly 1,500-person congress. A separately agreed 20–120-room delegation, exhibitor or organising-team block, or a small ancillary workshop using the six meeting rooms, is a sales hypothesis only—not published demand. Founex is outside central Geneva; validate acceptable transport and sustainable travel before offering rooms. This is an urban professional congress, not a demonstrated resort retreat. Banquet/catering scale is unverified and must not be promised.
findings.venueCommitments: Palexpo, Route François-Peyrot 30, 1218 Le Grand-Saconnex, Canton of Geneva, Switzerland. Territory classification: Geneva Airport / Palexpo corridor, not Founex/Nyon/La Côte and not downtown Geneva. The official September 2025 parliamentary motion states: “se tiendra du 13 au 16 juin à Palexpo”. It also identifies Maison communale de Plainpalais among the event sites. This is public venue identification, not proof of an executed venue contract; exact halls, satellite bookings and contractual terms remain unverified.
findings.historicalRotation: Verified rotation: Leipzig 2023 → Ghent 2024 → Gdańsk 2025 → Rimini 2026; announced Matsuyama/Ehime 2027 → Geneva 2028. Annual, different-city co-organisation is explicitly stated by the official FAQ, not merely inferred from adjacent years. No annual Geneva recurrence is established.
findings.accommodationSourcing: 2028 lodging sourcing is unconfirmed. No edition-specific housing bureau, booking portal, open hotel RFP, named host hotel, negotiated room block or hotel list was located in the English/French official material reviewed; therefore no 2028 incumbent hotels can be named. This is not evidence that inventory is open. K.I.T. Group Switzerland is the named PCO, but its accommodation contracting mandate is not published. The host release says “Further details on Velo-city 2028 will be announced in due course.” Palexpo separately advertises “pre-booking a number of rooms”; this is a generic service, not a Velo-city appointment or room commitment.
findings.organizationStructure: Association-led conference and exhibition: European Cyclists’ Federation (ECF) is the series owner/organiser; Geneva City and Canton are host partners. Geneva Tourism & Conventions / Convention Bureau led and coordinated the destination bid. K.I.T. Group Switzerland is the professional conference organiser, not the association owner. Palexpo is the identified venue, not thereby the lodging buyer. Geneva Tourism & Conventions describes itself as a private, officially recognised foundation.
findings.competitiveLimitations: No sourced sell-out, overflow requirement, competitor hotel allocation or hotel shortage was found. Palexpo’s published accommodation network is generic and cannot be converted into an incumbent list. The programme spans Palexpo and central-Geneva sites, creating a transport disadvantage for Founex (inference). Palexpo states Geneva-accommodation guests receive the Geneva Transport Card; applicability to this Vaud property is not established and should not be promised. The approximately 1,200 participants mentioned in a parliamentary report describes the series scale, whereas Switzerland Tourism lists 1,500 specifically against Geneva 2028; neither is a hotel-room requirement.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Approach Anouk Rey and Caroline Cerfontaine first, with David Cougoule as local routing contact. Ask who controls 2028 accommodation, whether an exclusive bureau or existing blocks apply, when hotel selection occurs, and whether a Vaud/Founex satellite can participate. Only after access is confirmed, propose a right-sized 20–120-room option or small ancillary meeting, with rates, transport/cycling arrangements and verified catering. Do not submit a whole-house or main-congress pitch. Use Mégane Simeon’s published contact for routing if necessary, not as evidence of purchasing authority.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: For the target 2028 edition, conference destination and Palexpo are already publicly identified, but hotel procurement access is unknown—not confirmed closed and not confirmed open. No published evidence shows that YOTEL is eligible for the official accommodation programme or that delegates will lodge toward La Côte. The source mentions airport/rail interfaces, not a confirmed arrival pattern or Founex room demand. Geneva is the activity location; Lausanne and French Pays de Gex are not verified event venues. Cross-border themes do not establish cross-border lodging.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: The capture window is the confirmed future Geneva 2028 edition, conditional on an accessible accommodation channel; do not relabel it as a speculative recurring Geneva cycle. Build an ECF/PCO relationship for selected delegation or ancillary needs, but later rotating-city editions are not automatically YOTEL opportunities. The FAQ says the 2029 host bid closed in September 2026; no later Geneva return is established.
